scope: Pure candidate policy describing a bounded future delegation ceiling above an unchanged delegation-disabled axiom-machine-principal.v1. It creates no delegation grant or runtime authority.
core_invariant: A candidate delegation policy is a proposal for future authority semantics, not authority. Current machine-principal v1 remains delegation.allowed=false/max_depth=0, and no child effect may be authorized from this candidate alone.

risks: candidate treated as if v1 delegation were enabled
runtime reads candidate instead of current machine-principal validator
controls: candidate requires a normalized v1 principal whose delegation is false/depth 0
all candidate sets must be subsets of v1 principal ceilings
all budgets must be <= v1 budgets

risks: spawned child interpreted as automatic authority
controls: future A3a attenuation must consume depth on every delegation
candidate expiry must be future at evaluation
candidate cannot outlive non-persistent machine principal

risks: policy digest treated as owner signature
controls: future authority-bearing layer must bind separate reviewed approval/currentness evidence

risks: A3a proof plus candidate treated as delegation record
controls: A3b remains a separate signed/current authority-bearing record

known_nonclaims: This candidate does not modify axiom-machine-principal.v1 or enable its delegation field.
This candidate does not bind owner/sponsor approval.
This candidate does not establish identity or revocation currentness.
This candidate does not create a child principal, grant, handoff or effect admission.
This candidate does not define capabilities/data classes beyond the existing v1 principal surface; A2/A3a remain responsible for richer authority projections.
This candidate does not modify the capability registry or supported runtime.
next_gates: review machine-principal v2 normative semantics rather than weakening v1
bind candidate policy to an explicit owner/sponsor approval artifact
combine approved parent policy with A3a attenuation proof into A3b signed delegation record
only then consider a separately reviewed runtime integration path
